edit.prompt: You are given TWO images. The FIRST image is a CONTROL MAP: solid GREEN regions are LAND, solid BLUE regions are SEA water. The SECOND image is a complete EXAMPLE MAP already drawn in the target art style: a bright, playful, colourful hand-illustrated fantasy map — cream/parchment land covered in little clustered pine and round trees, small rounded green hills, orange and tan ridge mountains; teal-blue sea drawn with fine darker concentric wave and depth lines and a crisp inked coastline with a thin pale beach. Redraw the FIRST image in the EXACT art style, colour palette, linework and shading of the SECOND image. CRITICAL: the LAND and SEA SHAPES — island positions, sizes and coastlines — come ENTIRELY from the FIRST control image. Put illustrated LAND in every GREEN region and SEA in every BLUE region, keeping the same islands and landmasses in the SAME positions, sizes and overall shapes as the control. Do NOT copy the islands, coastlines, continents or overall composition of the SECOND image — it is ONLY a style reference, not a map to reproduce. Draw ONLY natural terrain — trees, forests, hills, mountains, grassland, rocks, cliffs, beaches and sea. Do NOT draw any castles, keeps, forts, towers, houses, villages, tents, windmills, bridges or other buildings or man-made structures anywhere — those are added separately later; small sailing ships or sea creatures out on the open water are fine. This is a flat overhead map that fills the ENTIRE frame edge to edge — no horizon, no sky, no perspective, no empty margin, no labels, no text, no border. CRITICAL MAPPING: green control region becomes cream illustrated LAND, blue control region becomes teal SEA. Do not swap them.
